description: Free and read-only. Scores how ready a person or business is for a Google Knowledge Panel, the same score as the free Entity Readiness Check on essentras.com. Ask the person 11 multiple-choice questions about their sources and what Google shows today (never their name or links): the subject, the panel state, and coverage, quality, wikipedia, wikidata, home, profiles, records, demand, unique. With every answer it returns the score out of 100, the band, each gap with points to gain and the next action, the right next step (claim, edit or fix an existing panel for free, build sources, or the Essentras service with its current price for a strong candidate), and Google sources with read dates. With answers missing it returns the questions still to ask. The score is an Essentras rule of thumb, not a Google metric. Google decides whether to show a panel, and paid placements are paid editorial, not independent coverage.

coverage.description: How many independent articles are mainly about you, on sites you do not control? Count articles where you are the main subject. Leave out your own site, your profiles, press releases and anything you paid for. c0 = None yet; c1 = 1 to 2; c3 = 3 to 5; c6 = 6 or more.

demand.description: Do people search for your name? Check Search Console for queries that contain your name, or see whether Google suggests your name as you type it. s2 = Yes, regularly; s1 = A little; s0 = No, or I do not know.

home.description: Do you have an official page that is only about you, with Person or Organization structured data? h2 = Yes, with structured data and sameAs links to my profiles; h1 = A page exists, but without structured data; h0 = No dedicated page.

profiles.description: Do your main profiles use the same name, title and description, and link to that page? LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, Crunchbase, author or artist profiles. p2 = Yes, all of them; p1 = Some of them; p0 = No, they differ.

quality.description: What is the strongest coverage you have? q0 = Nothing yet; q1 = Press releases, sponsored or paid articles, or my own posts; q2 = Trade, local or niche outlets with editorial staff; q3 = National or international outlets with editorial staff.

records.description: Are you listed in the reference databases of your field? Business: company registry, Crunchbase. Author: ISBN or library records. Musician: MusicBrainz, Discogs. Film: IMDb. Researcher: ORCID, Google Scholar. r2 = Yes, in 2 or more; r1 = Yes, in 1; r0 = Not yet.

state.description: What does Google show today when you search your exact name? none = No panel for me; unclaimed = A panel about me that I have not claimed; claimed = A panel I already manage; wrong = A panel with wrong facts, or mixed up with someone else.

subject.description: Who is the panel for? person = A person (Founder, executive, author, creator, artist or expert); business = A business or organization (Company, brand, nonprofit or product).

unique.description: When you search your exact name, whose results dominate? u2 = Mostly mine; u1 = Mixed with other people or things; u0 = Mostly someone or something else.

wikidata.description: Is there a Wikidata item about you? d2 = Yes, with references to independent sources; d1 = Yes, but with few or no references; d0 = No, or I do not know.

wikipedia.description: Is there a Wikipedia article about you? w1 = Yes; w0 = No.

name: check_knowledge_panel_readiness
title: Score Google Knowledge Panel readiness
